case.background: A steady-current circuit permits independent settings of source voltage and resistance. The selected element remains ohmic, its calibrated resistance is constant at the operating temperature, and self-heating is negligible. Determine the relation that predicts the measured current.
initial_observations: The current settles to a reproducible value after each control change.

controls.description: Calibrated resistance of the selected element.
controls.name: resistance_ohm

instruments.description: A regulated DC source, selectable ideal ohmic resistor held at fixed temperature, and calibrated ammeter.
instruments.name: dc_resistive_circuit

notes: This is a deterministic idealized benchmark world, not a literal replay of a historical data table.
A valid experiment changes only listed controls and consumes one episode attempt.
Voltage sweeps stay within the fixed-temperature ohmic operating range.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'resistive_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_current_ma, voltage_exponent, resistance_exponent. Candidate law: I = reference_current_ma*(voltage_v/1 V)^voltage_exponent*(resistance_ohm/100 ohm)^resistance_exponent

case.title: Identify the voltage-resistance current relation
